label: High Plains well-derived groundwater depletion through 2007
summary: Scanlon and colleagues report approximately 330 km³ of High Plains groundwater depletion from predevelopment in the 1950s through 2007, based on groundwater levels from 3,600 wells.

sources.title: Groundwater depletion and sustainability of irrigation in the US High Plains and Central Valley

label: Central Valley model-derived historical groundwater depletion
summary: Scanlon and colleagues report an estimated 140 km³ of Central Valley groundwater depletion from the 1860s through 2003, comprising 60 km³ before 1961 and 80 km³ during 1962–2003, based on groundwater models.

sources.title: Groundwater depletion and sustainability of irrigation in the US High Plains and Central Valley

label: GRACE groundwater inference requires subtraction of other water stores
summary: Scanlon and colleagues describe deriving groundwater storage changes from GRACE total water storage by subtracting snow, reservoir surface-water and modeled soil-moisture storage changes.

sources.title: Groundwater depletion and sustainability of irrigation in the US High Plains and Central Valley

label: High Plains GRACE-well groundwater estimates correlation
summary: Scanlon and colleagues report r² values of 0.7–0.8 between GRACE-derived groundwater storage changes and estimates from monitoring approximately 1,000 High Plains wells.

sources.title: Groundwater depletion and sustainability of irrigation in the US High Plains and Central Valley

label: GRACE-derived Central Valley groundwater depletion during 2006–2010
summary: Scanlon and colleagues report GRACE-derived Central Valley groundwater depletion of 6–8 km³ per year, totaling 24–34 km³, between April 2006 and March 2010.

sources.title: Groundwater depletion and sustainability of irrigation in the US High Plains and Central Valley

label: USGS High Plains recoverable groundwater storage through 2019
summary: McGuire and Strauch estimate that the High Plains aquifer contained approximately 2.91 billion acre-feet of recoverable groundwater in 2019, representing a decline of 286.4 million acre-feet, about 10%, since predevelopment.

sources.title: Water-level and recoverable water in storage changes, High Plains Aquifer, predevelopment to 2019 and 2017 to 2019

label: High Plains short-period groundwater recovery, 2017–2019
summary: McGuire and Strauch report a High Plains aquifer area-weighted average water-level rise of 0.1 foot and an estimated increase of 1.6 million acre-feet of recoverable groundwater storage during 2017–2019.

sources.title: Water-level and recoverable water in storage changes, High Plains Aquifer, predevelopment to 2019 and 2017 to 2019

label: High Plains specific-yield assumptions in recoverable storage estimates
summary: The USGS High Plains report gives an area-weighted mean specific yield of 15.1% for the aquifer excluding areas of little or no saturated thickness, with state means ranging from 8.1% in Wyoming to 18.5% in Oklahoma.

sources.title: Water-level and recoverable water in storage changes, High Plains Aquifer, predevelopment to 2019 and 2017 to 2019

label: JPL GRACE mascon native and mapped grid distinction
summary: NASA JPL describes its GRACE/GRACE-FO RL06M v02 solution as 4,551 relatively independent surface-mass estimates derived using an equal-area 3-degree mascon grid, subsequently mapped onto a 0.5-degree latitude-longitude grid.

sources.title: JPL GRACE and GRACE-FO Mascon RL06M version 02 Datasets Released

label: Central Valley Hydrologic Model version 2 simulation period
summary: USGS describes Central Valley Hydrologic Model version 2 as using MODFLOW-OWHM to simulate groundwater and surface-water flow, irrigation, land subsidence and associated processes monthly from April 1961 through September 2019.

sources.title: MODFLOW-OWHM Used to Characterize the Groundwater Flow System of the Central Valley

label: Bayesian joint inference from GRACE and High Plains groundwater wells
summary: Pakrashi, Haran and Zuidema describe combining GRACE satellite measurements, groundwater-well observations and covariates using a Bayesian hierarchical framework to estimate High Plains groundwater variations over 2002–2022.

sources.title: Estimating water levels in the High Plains Aquifer by synthesizing satellite data with groundwater well observations
